evidence.note: National Guardian December 18,1961, printed/PDF page9, Jack A.Smith review of Reynolds’s The Forbidden Voyage explicitly gives July2 arrest after the June1958 Phoenix voyage into the nuclear test zone. Original scan visually inspected; identity matched by full name, Phoenix, Hiroshima work, August26,1958 verdict and subsequent appeal.

Original U.S.Attorneys Bulletin vol6 no24 printed698/PDF23 explicitly distinguishes August26,1958 verdict from September26,1958 sentence, two years with eighteen months suspended. Original scan visually inspected.

Friends Journal October18,1958 printed604/PDF12 independently confirms September26 sentence, six months plus eighteen months probation, and explicitly states $500 appeal bail continued. Original scan visually inspected. No actual prison start/end or served six months inferred.

Medford Mail Tribune Friday October21,1949 page1, United Press report individually names Eugene Dennis among defendants sentenced today by Judge Medina. Five-year Smith Act sentence distinguished from October14 verdict. Original dated masthead and report visually inspected.

Original Daily Iowan masthead is Tuesday July3,1951 despite archive filename di1951-07-01.pdf. Page1 Associated Press report individually names Eugene Dennis among seven who went behind bars Monday (July2); accompanying AP Wirephoto caption identifies him in prison van that Monday on transfer to federal house of detention. Original masthead, report and caption visually inspected. This actual Smith Act prison-entry date does not apply to his separate contempt-of-Congress case.
